steps.message: Build succeeds. Here's the final diff:

## Diagnosis

The filter indicator ("Showing 9 of 15 satellites (show all)") lives in `GPSTest/src/main/res/layout/gps_status.xml` (`status_filter_group`) and is only ever toggled inside `GpsStatusFragment.updateFilterView()`, which is called from the satellite-status update path (`updateGnssStatus()`/`updateListVisibility()`).

When GNSS is stopped, `onGnssStopped()` → `setStarted(false)` clears all the status views (lat/lon, TTFF, sat count, adapters, etc.) but never touched the filter group. Since no further satellite status callbacks arrive after stopping, `updateFilterView()` is never called again, so the stale filter text (and the italic typeface on the satellite count view) stayed on screen.

## Fix

In `GpsStatusFragment`:

1. Extracted the "hide filter" logic from `updateFilterView()` into a new `hideFilterView()` helper (hides `filterGroup` and restores the normal typeface on `mNumSats`), with null guards in case views aren't inflated yet.
2. Called `hideFilterView()` from the `!navigating` branch of `setStarted()`, alongside the other view resets, so stopping GNSS clears the filter text.

Behavior is otherwise preserved: the user's GNSS filter preference itself is untouched, and once GNSS is restarted the next satellite status update calls `updateFilterView()`, which re-shows the text if a filter is still active.

The project builds successfully (`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` with JDK 11 — the Gradle 6.1.1 wrapper can't run on the default JDK 17 in this environment).
